title: Crisis Response Mesh
outcome: Coordinate rapid diagnosis and action during outages, safety events, or urgent operations
breakthrough: The ecosystem can form an instant incident team
lane: Mission dispatch, execution visibility, and real-time operations

phases.name: Phase 1 - Build the Crisis Response Mesh Core

subphases.name: 1.1 Crisis Response Mesh Domain Model and State Plane
work: Define typed nodes, topology, capabilities, routes, and synchronization state required to coordinate rapid diagnosis and action during outages, safety events, or urgent operations, with explicit versions and validation at every boundary.

Implement an owned persistent state layer optimized for live missions, dispatch, routes, priorities, locations, events, and multi-agent traffic; include snapshots or event history when state changes over time.
Expose create, query, update, subscribe, and delete operations through local APIs plus an SDK that never requires private cross-runtime imports.

subphases.name: 1.2 Crisis Response Mesh Execution Runtime
work: Build resumable workers and state machines that perform the core operation: coordinate rapid diagnosis and action during outages, safety events, or urgent operations.
Add cancellation, idempotency, bounded retries, timeouts, quotas, sandbox limits, and deterministic recovery from partial failure.
Create a local simulator that can replay success, malformed inputs, disconnection, overload, provider loss, and restart recovery.

phases.name: Phase 2 - Make Crisis Response Mesh Adaptive and Usable

subphases.name: 2.1 Crisis Response Mesh Decision and Learning Engine
work: Implement scoring, planning, prediction, search, or optimization using matching, route optimization, event processing, queue theory, and crisis simulation.
Create feedback signals from task outcomes and user corrections; update tunable behavior without silently changing hard safety limits.
Return confidence, alternatives, bottlenecks, and a concise machine-readable explanation for every important automated choice.

subphases.name: 2.2 Crisis Response Mesh Interaction Surface
work: Build the primary experience in the mission cockpit, real-time map, dispatch board, and operations replay room, including live state, controls, errors, and recovery actions.
Add a CLI and typed client library so humans, agents, games, and third-party applications can operate the capability directly.
Stream progress and intermediate artifacts in real time so long operations remain inspectable, interruptible, and steerable.

phases.name: Phase 3 - Scale Crisis Response Mesh into a Breakthrough Product

subphases.name: 3.1 Crisis Response Mesh Offline, Edge, and Cloud Mesh
work: Implement local-only, hybrid, and cloud execution with explicit capability discovery and graceful behavior when optional peers disappear.
Add conflict-safe synchronization, workload placement, caching, backpressure, and failover across devices or nodes where the feature benefits from distribution.
Benchmark latency, throughput, memory, energy, network transfer, and cost; make the scheduler choose the best execution mode from measured constraints.

subphases.name: 3.2 Crisis Response Mesh Signature Breakthrough
work: Implement the differentiating behavior: The ecosystem can form an instant incident team. Ship it as an opt-in executable mode, not a mockup.
Run adversarial, load, privacy, misuse, degraded-network, and recovery tests against the novel behavior; block unsafe automatic actions.
Package the feature as an independently installable capability with a live demo, sample integration, metrics endpoint, and rollback-safe release artifact.
